comment: Firmware inventory extraction: the read-only GET /api/firmware and its helpers move from server.js to routes/firmwareInventory.js. Executed only with the owner's OK to Dev, mechanically by tools/refactor/codemods/extract-firmware-inventory.js (one contiguous slice; one declared rewrite, PRINTERS -> getPrinters()). EXCLUDED, by the owner's ruling, and untouched: everything about firmware DEPLOYMENT — /api/firmware-files, /api/firmware-inspect, /api/firmware-deploy, /api/firmware-options, /api/firmware-stop, /api/firmware-status, /api/firmware-deploy-status and their state (FW_STATE, FW_QUEUE, FW_RUNNING, FW_STOP_REQUESTED, FW_JOBS, fwBusyWith, fwDraining, firmwareTargetFor, firmwareDeployBlockedBy, runFirmwareDeploy, drainFirmwareQueue, …). The codemod refuses if the moved text reads any FW_* name other than its own FW_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, and checks all seven deployment routes are in server.js exactly once before and after.
baseNote: On the batch branch (refactor/batch-snapshot-firmware) the baseline pins commit is 68f2293. The same change exists as 920ef18 on the standalone branch refactor/firmware-inventory; 920ef18 is NOT an ancestor of the batch branch and must never be used as a reset target here. See verifiedBaseline (standalone), integrationBaseline (batch) and extractionParent.
sourceRange: One contiguous slice of server.js at the base: lines 4450-4597 (148 lines). 4450-4455: the "// ---- Firmware inventory (same Moonraker APIs fluidd reads) ----" header comment and its blank line; 4456-4464: firmwareTabEligible with its comment; 4465-4471: FW_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS with its comment; 4472-4514: probeFirmware with its comment; 4515-4597: app.get("/api/firmware", requireAuth, …). The block ends directly before the blank line and the "// ---- Health diagnostics: GET /api/health and its helpers live in" registration, which stays byte-identical (checked by the codemod). The three names (firmwareTabEligible, FW_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, probeFirmware) are used nowhere else in server.js or routes/ (grep-verified at the base).

injected.getPrinters: () => PRINTERS — server.js:98 `let CFG, FOLDER, PRINTERS;`, reassigned by loadConfig and the config routes (lines 125, 251, 265, 282); policy rule 4
injected.probeCached: server.js:2951 function (hoisted; the authoritative probe — test/fleetProbe.test.js pins its callers)
injected.how: parameters of registerFirmwareInventoryRoutes(app, { requireAuth, getPrinters, printerVisibleTo, getConnector, getCapabilities, probeCached }). firmwareTabEligible, probeFirmware and the route use injected names, so they are declared inside registerFirmwareInventoryRoutes (indented by 2); FW_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, a pure constant, stays at module scope with its comment. No module-level dependency slots. The moved code reads PRINTERS twice (the single read's PRINTERS[idx], the list's PRINTERS.map) and no CFG, FOLDER or USERS.

exports: module.exports = { registerFirmwareInventoryRoutes } — nothing else. registerFirmwareInventoryRoutes returns nothing. No `_internal`: no existing test needs the helpers by name through the module (test/firmwareInventory.test.js extracts probeFirmware and firmwareTabEligible from the source TEXT and keeps doing so with loader-only edits), and the new pins exercise them through the route only.
strictMode: routes/firmwareInventory.js has no "use strict" (server.js is sloppy mode; semantics kept identical).

moduleState.constants: FW_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS at module scope; a number, no timers, no Maps, no I/O at creation. The boundary owns no mutable state (the 20 s timer is per call, created and cleared inside probeFirmware).
moduleState.registration: server.js requires the module and calls registerFirmwareInventoryRoutes(app, {...}) at the moved block's original position (replacing lines 4450-4597), directly before the Health registration, so the Express route order and the require order are unchanged (bed-temp route, firmware inventory, health, sync…). Function declarations that were hoisted to server.js's top level (firmwareTabEligible, probeFirmware) now exist from registration on; nothing outside the block references them (grep-verified), so this is unobservable — stated for the Guardian.

declaredHarnessNotes.test/firmwareDeploy.test.js: lines 723-724 only. The file's serverSrc (server.js) is used by every other test in it for deployment code that stays in server.js, so it is not changed; this one slice — the single-printer read's visibility check — reads routes/firmwareInventory.js instead (fs and path are already required by the file). Base: from the route's start to the Health comment = the route. Head: from the route's start to its own "\n  });\n" = the route. Both assertions on it are unchanged.
declaredHarnessNotes.test/connectorCoreMethods.test.js: line 29: routes/firmwareInventory.js joins the scanned sources. Without it the generated test "server.js checks a connector has getFirmwareInfo() before calling it" would still be generated and pass on server.js's OTHER getFirmwareInfo call (rediscovery, `conn.capabilities.firmwareInfo && conn.getFirmwareInfo`), silently no longer covering probeFirmware's call and guard.
declaredHarnessNotes.test/helpers/firmwareInventoryCode.js: declared helper (Guardian reviews every line): only the header comment, the SERVER→MODULE constant, the unused routeEnd import and loadSource() change. Base: slices server.js into the sandbox, where app/requireAuth/printerVisibleTo/getConnector/getCapabilities/probeCached are globals and PRINTERS is a global read through to world.printers. Head: runs routes/firmwareInventory.js in the sandbox with a require() that refuses everything, requires the exports to be exactly registerFirmwareInventoryRoutes, calls it with the same fakes as parameters and getPrinters: () => world.printers, and requires it to return nothing. test/firmwareInventoryBehaviour.test.js is not changed.
declaredHarnessNotes.test/fleetProbe.test.js: NOT changed. Its caller pin ("every module: only the fleet route uses the display path…") already scans routes/ and names callers by their enclosing function, so probeFirmware is found in routes/firmwareInventory.js under the same name and the expected list is identical.

contractNotes: firmware-inventory.json: 22 requests, each with a declared expectation (status; record count for the streams), 2 fake-printer control steps, a reload and a restart. The fixture has no flashable printer (all three are klipper-moonraker: firmwareInfo yes, firmwareDeploy no), so the list is [] and the stream is exactly 2 records for every user; the single-printer read reaches the fake printer (queryFirmwareInfo). trackDelays adds 20000 (FW_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS) to the 25 s Health deadline: created/cleared/fired counts per process start are compared. health.json and smoke.json unchanged. Nothing new is declared volatile.
packaging: Dockerfile already has `COPY routes ./routes` (added for Health); pkg follows the require graph (no pkg.scripts entry: not a worker); test/docker.test.js walks server.js's require graph and sees routes/firmwareInventory.js under the existing COPY. No package.json or Dockerfile change. Policy rule 8: real Docker + pkg builds (V12) remain mandatory before deployment, each download/build owner-approved.

rollback.afterCommit: Firmware inventory extraction only, on the batch branch: `git revert 725388d` (keeps history). The resulting application and test files equal those of 80b90a9, the verified integration baseline. On the standalone branch: `git revert 73710a6`.
rollback.wholeBatch: Whole batch (Snapshot and Firmware inventory extractions with all their preparation): return to e5cbe420ecf66b23efb69d6d430583d87ac01ceb, the production commit the batch was built on.
rollback.snapshotOnly: UNVERIFIED: reverting only the Snapshot extraction (85d833d) while keeping the Firmware inventory extraction produces a tree that was never built, tested or reviewed. Do not use it as a rollback without verifying it first.
rollback.notThis: Never move the batch branch to the standalone commits (920ef18, 73e4ccb, 73710a6): they are not ancestors of it, and doing so would discard the Snapshot extraction and the integration history.
rollback.never: production main is not touched by any of this; it changes only through a separate release decision

knownToolingLimitations: the LIST is empty in the container harness: no fixture printer declares firmwareDeploy (the fixture is fixed), so list rows, their decoration, the batches of 6 and the per-batch stream records are pinned in-process only (test/firmwareInventoryBehaviour.test.js)

the single-printer read against the fake printer has klipper: null and mcus[].version: null: the fake answers 404 to /printer/info and its mcu object has no mcu_version (setting one through /__control/set cannot be undone, so it is not set); machine/firmware/software/os are exercised once through the existing systemInfo control
contract expectations can declare only a status and an NDJSON record count; the answers' content is compared between runs (base ×2 vs head), not against a declared value
disconnect handling is pinned in-process only (the harness client cannot abort a request)
the 20 s timeout firing is pinned in-process only, with a manual timer (the harness has no printer that accepts a request and never answers); in the harness the timer is only ever created and cleared

a plain 'timeout removed' mutation is not declared: with it the pre-existing regression test in test/firmwareInventory.test.js never finishes (its own documented failure mode) and a verification run would wait for its time limit; route-timeout-removed removes the timeout on the only path the route uses and is detected by the new pins
concurrency inside a batch is pinned as 'six start before any answers; the seventh starts only after all six have' — not the wall-clock behaviour
the connectors' own getFirmwareInfo implementations and their 5 s request timeouts are not pinned here (connectors do not move)

compareRuns compares logs, files written and audit rows between base1 and head only, and consults base2 for printer requests only when base1 and head differ (recorded 2026-11-16 for Discover; unchanged)
